description: Cross-method constraint quality metrics for SICA vs ICG vs Contrastive vs Debate on FOLIO-204 (Mistral-7B)

notes.parse_rate: 97.1% of 2448 traces (12/question) yielded extractable constraints. 96.5% of unique constraints compiled in Z3.
notes.redundancy: 42.9% of raw constraints are duplicates across traces — direct evidence of co-sourcing. Multi-trace sampling produces overlapping constraint sets.
notes.discriminative: No per-candidate Z3 evaluation stored. Proxy: 81.4% of questions had MaxSAT scores supporting >1 candidate answer (constraint set differentiates answers at question level).
notes.trivially_sat: Not computable. SICA evaluates all constraints as a unified MaxSAT problem, not per-candidate.

notes.parse_rate: 74.6% of traces produced non-empty constraint sets. But those that compiled had 99.4% Z3 success — highest among all methods.
notes.redundancy: 32.3% redundancy, lower than SICA's 42.9%. ICG's independent generation produces more diverse constraints per trace.
notes.discriminative: Proxy: 77.0% questions with multi-answer scores (vs SICA 81.4%).
notes.unique_per_q: 24.9 unique constraints/question vs SICA's 39.3 — fewer but cleaner constraints.

notes.parse_rate: 74.0% of questions yielded any constraints. Z3 compile rate 94.4% (pro: 92.5%, con: 96.7%).
notes.unique_per_q: 9.2 constraints/question — much lower than SICA/ICG because constraints are targeted (pro/con for specific candidates).
notes.discriminative: 51.0% of questions had constraints that produced different contrastive scores across candidates. Lower than SICA/ICG proxies.
notes.trivially_sat: 62.7% of questions had ALL pro constraints satisfied across ALL candidates — these pro constraints don't help distinguish answers.
notes.redundancy: 0% redundancy by design: constraints are per-candidate, no cross-candidate dedup applied.

notes.mechanism: Debate uses proposer/critic/defense debates + independent traces. No symbolic Z3 constraints.
notes.parse_rate: 81.3% = (valid_debates + traces_with_answer) / total. Valid debates: 63.1%, trace answers: 87.3%.
notes.unique_per_q: 13.0 valid reasoning units/question (valid debates + answered traces). NOT Z3 constraints.
notes.discriminative: Not applicable — debate mechanism does not produce per-candidate Z3 evaluations.

summary_table.footnote: * = proxy metric: % questions where MaxSAT scores support >1 candidate answer. Debate unique/q counts reasoning units, not Z3 constraints.

key_findings: SICA produces the most constraints (39.3 unique/q) with highest trace yield (97.1%), but 42.9% redundancy confirms co-sourcing across traces.
ICG has fewer constraints (24.9/q) with lower trace yield (74.6%), but highest Z3 compile rate (99.4%) and lower redundancy (32.3%) — cleaner, more diverse constraints.
Contrastive generates fewest constraints (9.2/q) and only 51% of questions have discriminative power. 62.7% trivially satisfied — pro constraints often don't help distinguish candidates.
Debate produces no symbolic constraints. 63.1% of debates are 'valid' (proposer and critic disagree). Combined with traces, 81.3% of reasoning units produce usable answers.

discriminative_ratio and trivially_satisfied_ratio are only directly computable for Contrastive (which stores per-candidate Z3 eval results). SICA/ICG use unified MaxSAT without per-candidate breakdown.
